goal: Beat the previous best steady-state OUT-OF-CORE throughput of srsvd-jax on ONE L40S, 100 iterations of implement-then-measure. The record metric is STEADY5_GB: gigabytes of a FIXED 1.546 TB synthetic store (2.05x the node's RealMemory) consumed by the END-TO-END pipeline (node-local NVMe O_DIRECT read -> host -> PCIe -> device kernel) inside a 300 s steady-state window that excludes process start, compile and warm-up, at a FIXED algorithm (k=32 p=10 q=2, 3 passes) with the numerics gate passing. Every candidate is judged against the champion re-measured in the same iteration; the work may lie in srsvd-jax or in the end-to-end pipeline (bench, reader, host path, JAX usage).

The host side of this pipeline is finished.

claims.claim: --sync-every 4 is a NULL-BELOW-FLOOR at +0.579 pct median, not the +1.43 pct iteration 15's single row suggested. The effect is real in sign but under both the 0.6319 pct floor and the contract's 1 pct minimum. It belongs to the FLAG and not to the pool the flag derives -- the same pool at sync_every 1 returns -0.10 pct and leaves 5 of 8 buffers never resident -- and its mechanism is NOT the sync_wait it removes, which is an order of magnitude too small; the time comes out of the read phase and is unexplained.

claims.claim: --depth 4 --sync-every 4 IS THE CHAMPION at 10326.326340 STEADY5_GB, established by a strictly alternated A/B/A/B/A/B design: median-of-medians +1.2015 pct, mean-of-means +1.2809 pct, paired differences +1.1759/+1.3896/+1.2772 pct all clearing 1 pct individually, populations disjoint by 120 GB, both arm spreads below the 0.2196 pct floor. 2.538x the origin and 93.9 pct of the read roof. The iteration-17 block-design objection is answered in the OPPOSITE direction: the baseline drifts downward, so the block design understated rather than inflated. Mechanism still unexplained -- the sync_wait it removes is ~20x too small and the gain is in read_s.

claims.evidence: Iteration 19, alternated under numactl --interleave=all at --convert-threads 8. Champion arm 10323.151334/10317.199533/10327.123473 (median 10323.151334, spread 0.0961 pct). Paired differences: d6s4 -0.8165 pct, d4s8 -2.8928 pct, d6s8 -3.7986 pct; additivity -0.8165 + -2.8928 = -3.709 predicted vs -3.7986 observed. sync_wait as pct of span falls 0.045 -> 0.033 (job 0) and 0.026 -> 0.015 (job 1) going from sync-every 4 to 8 while throughput falls 2.89 pct. read_wait_s exactly 0.000000 in all 18 jobs; read_s rises 129.5-130.7 -> 131.0-132.1 -> 133.9-135.6 -> 135.2-136.6 s.
claims.claim: --depth 4 --sync-every 4 is a LOCAL OPTIMUM, a peak: depth 6 costs 0.82 pct, sync-every 8 costs 2.89 pct, and the two penalties are additive to within 0.09 pct. AND sync_wait IS FALSIFIED AS THE MECHANISM -- halving it again makes throughput worse, so it moves in the same direction as the metric and cannot be the cause. The entire difference lives in read_s with the reader never starved. The mechanism of the d4s4 gain remains unknown.

claims.claim: The knob optimum is fully mapped. --sync-every 4 is a SHARP optimum (-0.54 pct at 3, -2.89 pct at 8). --depth is a FLAT TOP spanning 3, 4 and 5 (all NULLs against each other) with cliffs at 2 (-0.69 pct) and 6 (-0.82 pct). Depth 4 is kept because 3 and 5 tie it and 5 costs more staging. The 2x2 factorial d2s1/d2s4/d4s1/d4s4 is complete with every cell a same-iteration alternated measurement; the iteration-15 d4s1 cross-iteration estimate of +0.09 pct was overturned by measurement at -1.1240 pct.

claims.evidence: Iteration 20: sync_wait is flat to the millisecond across depth 3/4/5 (0.0347-0.0602 s, job-position-matched within 1 ms) while read_s moves up to 0.55 s; d4s3 is the first row where sync_wait RISES (+0.007 to +0.010 s = 0.008 pct) against a 0.544 pct loss; wire_pool_pin_s rises monotonically with depth (2.224 to 2.731 s) while throughput does not fall, and d5 has the highest pin cost of any row and ties the champion. Iteration 19: sync_wait fell while throughput fell. read_wait_s exactly 0.000000 in all 18 jobs of both iterations.
claims.claim: The mechanism of the depth/sync-every effect is NOT sync_wait (now excluded in both directions, and two orders of magnitude too small either way) and NOT pin cost (positively excluded by d5). 100 pct of every measured difference lives in read_s with the reader never starved. The mechanism remains unknown after three iterations of trying to name it.

claims.evidence: Iteration 21 completed 2x2, all cells same-iteration alternated, relative to d4s4: d2s1 -1.2015 pct (iter18, n=3 vs n=3), d2s4 -0.6940 pct, d4s1 -1.1240 pct, d4s4 reference (n=3 median 10310.526019, spread 0.1010 pct). Depth 2->4 is +0.6940 pct at sync-every 4 and +0.0775 pct at sync-every 1; sync-every 1->4 is +1.1240 pct at depth 4 and +0.5075 pct at depth 2. Interaction 0.6940-0.0775 = 1.1240-0.5075 = 0.6165 pct, identical down both paths. Naive additive prediction +1.8180 pct vs actual +1.2015 pct.
claims.claim: --depth and --sync-every are NOT additive at the optimum: they INTERACT with a +0.6165 pct term and only pay together. Deep buffering with per-block syncing buys essentially nothing (+0.08 pct); coarse syncing with shallow buffering buys less than half its potential (+0.51 pct). This reconciles with iteration 19's far-field additivity -- additivity is a property of the tails, not the peak -- and it retires the campaign's earlier framing of the champion as 'depth 4 beats depth 2'. The interaction is OVER-DETERMINED: computable two ways, agreeing to four decimals.
